Bold text generator

Most places that won't let you bold text — Instagram captions, your X bio, a LinkedIn post, a Discord message that doesn't take markdown — will happily display 𝗯𝗼𝗹𝗱 𝗨𝗻𝗶𝗰𝗼𝗱𝗲. That's what this does: it swaps your letters for the bold mathematical alphanumerics, in the clean sans flavor (𝗹𝗶𝗸𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀) and the chunkier serif one (𝐥𝐢𝐤𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬), with bold italic and bold script also in the dropdown. Bold sans is the safest of all the styles on this site — if any fancy text is going to render in an app, it's this one — which is why it's the first one to reach for when something is being picky. It does have numbers and basic digits, unlike most decorative styles. Worth knowing: this is for short bits, not paragraphs.

How to use it

Type in the box on the left. The style you’ve picked on the right updates as you type — no “generate” button. Click Copy and paste it wherever you need. On the home page you can also browse every style in the list below and click any row to load it into the panel.

Where it renders, and where it breaks

Bold is the workhorse. It renders in more places than any other style here, but a couple of profile fields still strip it.

App / platformWhereStatusNotes
Instagrambio, captions, comments, username (often)WorksBold sans frequently survives even in the @username field — rare for a fancy style. Bio and captions always work.
TikTokbio, captions, commentsWorksFine. Username field is stricter but bold sans is your best shot at it.
Discordmessages, nicknames, About Me, statusWorksWorks everywhere. Use Discord's own **markdown** inside messages; use this for nicknames, statuses and bots that ignore markdown.
X (Twitter)posts, bio, display nameWorksAll fine. The @handle is still plain-only.
LinkedInposts, headlinePartialPosts and the headline usually keep bold (sans more often than serif). Some other profile fields strip it — check after pasting.
WhatsApp / Telegrammessages, status, AboutWorksWorks. WhatsApp also has its own *bold* with asterisks in messages; this is for the places that one doesn't reach.
Games (Roblox, Fortnite, Free Fire…)in-game namesWorksBold sans is the style most likely to pass a game's name filter. If even bold bounces, the filter is rejecting non-ASCII entirely.

All of these are real Unicode characters, not images or font files, so the styling travels with the text wherever you paste it. The catch: a few apps with locked-down fonts will draw some glyphs as empty boxes — that's the receiving app, not the text, and switching styles fixes it. Bold (sans), Small Caps and Full-width render the widest. Checked May 2026; platforms change their font handling constantly, so treat the table below as a strong guide, not a guarantee. Examples & use cases

Bold is for emphasis, not body text. Where it does the job:

  • Section headers in a flat editor — 𝗦𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗼𝗻𝗲 stands out in tools that don't show real headings in certain views — task lists, simple notes, some wikis.
  • The one word that matters in a post — Bolding a single key word — 𝗳𝗿𝗲𝗲, 𝗻𝗼𝘄, 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀 — pulls the eye without rewriting the whole sentence.
  • Instagram username (yes, really) — Bold sans is the rare fancy style that often passes Instagram's @username filter. Worth a try before settling for plain.
  • Game / Discord name — Clean, legible at small sizes, and the most filter-friendly. 𝗽𝗹𝗮𝘆𝗲𝗿_𝟬𝟭 — digits work too.
  • Bold + italic together — Pick Bold italic from the dropdown for 𝙗𝙤𝙩𝙝 𝙖𝙩 𝙤𝙣𝙘𝙚, or bold script if you want bold and cursive in one.

Common mistakes

  • Don't bold a whole paragraph. It's tiring to read and some screen readers announce each character individually. Bold a header, a name, or a word — not a block of text.
  • Don't confuse sans bold with serif bold. Sans bold (𝗯𝗼𝗹𝗱) is cleaner and renders more reliably across apps; serif bold (𝐛𝐨𝐥𝐝) is heavier and more old-fashioned. When in doubt, pick sans — it boxes out the least.
  • Don't use it on your website for emphasis. Search engines and screen readers see math characters, not bold text. Use real HTML <strong> there. This is for apps that give you no formatting at all.
  • Don't expect Discord markdown to work in a nickname. **this** works in messages, not in nicknames, statuses or many bots. That's exactly where a Unicode bold is useful — paste it in.

FAQ

Does bold text work on LinkedIn?
In posts and the headline, usually yes. LinkedIn occasionally strips it from certain profile fields, so check after pasting. Bold sans survives more often than bold serif.
Sans-serif bold or serif bold — which should I pick?
Sans bold (𝗯𝗼𝗹𝗱) is cleaner and renders more reliably across apps. Serif bold (𝐛𝐨𝐥𝐝) is heavier and a bit more old-fashioned. When in doubt, sans.
Is this bad for accessibility?
For a word or a name, it's fine. For long passages it's a real problem — some screen readers announce each character individually, e.g. "mathematical bold small a, mathematical bold small b...". Keep it to short, intentional bits.
Can I bold and italicize at once?
Yes — the Bold italic style in the dropdown does both. There's also a bold script option if you want bold and cursive together.
Do numbers work in bold text?
Yes — bold has a full set of digits (𝟬–𝟵 for sans, 𝟎–𝟗 for serif), unlike script, italic and most decorative styles. So a bold username with numbers in it works.
Why is bold the "safest" style?
The bold mathematical alphanumerics are some of the most widely-implemented characters outside plain ASCII — almost every modern font includes them. If any fancy style is going to render in a given app, bold sans is the one. It's the fallback to try when everything else boxes out.
